reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Evidence shows target engagement through immune responses detected by ELISPOT assay. Biomarker data confirms tumor-antigen-specific immunity was induced, with differential responses between arms (1/13 vs 5/27 responders in PBMC, 1/13 vs 8/27 in sentinel nodes with p=0.004). 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Downstream immune biology was modulated as evidenced by the immune response biomarkers, particularly strong in the GM-CSF arm with significant sentinel node responses (p=0.004). The mechanism of immune costimulation was engaged. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite confirmed target engagement and pathway modulation, clinical translation failed. Overall response rate was only 7.5% (3/40 patients with partial responses), well below clinically meaningful thresholds. No complete responses were observed in either arm. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup differences in clinical response, though GM-CSF arm showed superior immune responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major confounders - adequate duration (104 weeks), reasonable sample size, appropriate endpoints measured.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear evidence of target engagement and immune pathway activation (significant sentinel node responses p=0.004, detectable PBMC responses) but clinical endpoint failed with only 7.5% response rate and no complete responses
